subject: WRITE statement
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB691). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 "If the organization of the write file is sequential, format 1 shall be specified" => OK 2). The rule is a FORMAT-SELECTION rule, and what it forbids is read off the formats: Format 1 (sequential) of 14.9.51.2 carries no INVALID KEY bracket at all -- only Format 2 (random) does -- so a WRITE on a sequential-organization file may not carry the phrase. It was PARSED AND DROPPED: SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite never read the statement's INVALID KEY family of conditionalPhrases, so the program compiled clean at every edition and NEITHER imperative ran, with no diagnostic on either severity axis. Measured with a CLI probe before the fix (WRITE ... INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-IK" NOT INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-NIK" on ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL printed only 'DONE 00' at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive), not inferred. It is the THIRD arm of one silent drop: PB144 screened REWRITE (SR-14.9.35.3-2), PB334 READ, and this one hid because the INVALID KEY phrase was consumed by the KEYED binder only. Now screened through the ONE severity seam (StatementValidation.ScreenForbiddenPhrase -> COBOL1720, no new code): an ERROR under strict at all four editions, a WARNING under --permissive -- and, unlike the REWRITE arm as PB144 left it, the phrase is BOUND rather than dropped, because 9.1.14's final rule item 2 (cite.py --check 9.1.14 "If the I-O status indicates a successful completion, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement or to the imperative-statement specified in the NOT INVALID KEY phrase if it is specified" => OK 2)) gives the NOT INVALID KEY imperative a live meaning even here. The INVALID arm is provably dead on this organization: 9.1.13.5's four invalid-key statuses '21'-'24' each name a relative or indexed file, so the emitter's status-first '2' branch can never fire -- dead, never rerouted. D9 CORPUS SWEEP RUN, NOT REASONED: a record-name -> FD -> SELECT organization mapping over all 459 NIST programs finds 77 WRITE ... INVALID KEY sites, every one of them on an INDEXED or RELATIVE file and ZERO on a sequential-organization file; all 459 then compiled at --std 85 with the screened compiler and NOT ONE drew COBOL1720; and the ~Nist conformance leg is byte-identical across the change (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 352, Total: 352, before and after). The screen is edition-invariant by construction (Removed keys on Permissive, never on edition) and measured so at 85/2002/2014/2023.
